transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve messed everything up at work and that everyone can see how worthless I am, like it’s all being recorded as proof. It's just this constant, heavy weight, and I feel completely overwhelmed by it.
Can you tell me more about these feelings of being worthless and if you've experienced any physical symptoms like palpitations, sweating, or trembling when these thoughts occur?

I'm convinced I'm the worst person on my team, and that every mistake I've ever made is being compiled on a hidden server to prove how incompetent I am. I don't really have shaking or sweating, but my body just feels incredibly heavy and slowed down, like I'm trying to move through molasses with a weight on my chest.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your interest in activities you once enjoyed, or have you noticed a decrease in your energy levels over the past few weeks?

I used to love playing softball and going to salsa classes, but now I just cancel on my friends and sit on the couch because even putting on my shoes feels pointless. I also feel completely drained all the time; even simple things like walking to the kitchen or standing during a short meeting at work totally wipe me out.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of worthlessness and lack of energy, and have they been constant or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?

This has been going on constantly for about four months, starting right after a major cheating investigation at work. It's been pretty heavy and constant, though on the rare days when my mood lifts even a little bit, the whispering voice and the feeling of being recorded fade a bit too.

Have you had any previous episodes like this in your life before the cheating investigation at work, or is this the first time you've experienced such intense feelings of worthlessness and lack of energy?

No, this is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this in my life. Before that investigation at work, I had never felt this kind of intense depression, worthlessness, or extreme lack of energy. It is all completely new to me.

Can you describe if there was a specific event or stressor, like the cheating investigation at work, that seemed to trigger these feelings, and if so, how you think it might be connected to your current state?

Yes, it definitely started with that high-profile cheating investigation about four months ago, where I was terrified I had missed key cues on the monitors. That worry quickly spiraled into a constant fear that the cameras were actually watching me and recording my mistakes to prove my incompetence. It triggered this deep, heavy depression and left me feeling completely exhausted and worthless.

You mentioned this has been your first episode of feeling this way, lasting about four months, but can you tell me if you've had any periods, even brief, where you felt completely back to your normal self during this time, or has it been a persistent feeling of depression and worthlessness?

No, I haven't felt completely back to my normal self at all; it has been a persistent, heavy cloud for the last four months. On the rare days when my mood lightens just a tiny bit, the whispering voice and the feeling of being recorded fade slightly, but the overall darkness has never fully lifted.

You've mentioned that this has been your first episode and it's lasted about four months, but can you clarify if there have been any significant variations in the intensity of your symptoms over this period, or have they remained relatively consistent?

They have been mostly consistent and very heavy over the last four months. On the rare days when my mood lightens slightly, the whispering voice and the feeling of being recorded fade a bit into the background, but overall it has been a continuous, exhausting stretch.

Given that you've experienced this intense depression for about four months without feeling completely back to normal, can you tell me if you've had any previous episodes of depression that might have been less severe or shorter, even if they didn't seem significant at the time?
No, I don't recall ever having any previous episodes of depression, even minor ones. This is the absolute first time I've ever felt this way in my life. Before this, I was always active and outgoing.

You mentioned that on rare days when your mood lightens slightly, the whispering voice and feeling of being recorded fade into the background; can you describe what typically happens on those days that makes you feel slightly better?
I'm really not sure what makes those days slightly better, to be honest. There isn't any specific trigger or event that happens; the mood just seems to lift a tiny bit completely at random.
Can you think of anything that you do differently on those rare days when your mood lifts slightly, or is it purely the absence of the heavy feelings that makes them stand out?

I don't really do anything differently on those days since I'm still completely exhausted. They just stand out because the heavy sadness lifts slightly, and most importantly, the whispering voices and the feeling that everything is being recorded against me fade into the background.

You've had this persistent episode of depression for about four months without feeling completely back to normal; do you think that if the situation at work were to resolve, such as the cheating investigation being fully cleared, you might start feeling better, or do you feel like your depression has become somewhat independent of the initial trigger?

Even if that specific investigation were cleared, I feel like the damage is already done and this has grown much bigger than just that one event. I'm still completely consumed by guilt over every past mistake I've ever made. It feels like I can't just snap out of it now, no matter what happens at work.

Do you think your current state could potentially improve if you were to experience a significant change in your work environment or a resolution to the issues that initially triggered these feelings, or do you believe your depression has taken on a life of its own regardless of external factors?

I really feel like this depression has taken on a life of its own now, and it's far too late for a change in work to fix anything. Because I've already permanently messed everything up and feel completely worthless, a new environment wouldn't lift this heavy weight. It just stays with me constantly, no matter what is happening around me.

Given that you've experienced this intense depression for about four months without previous episodes, do you think this current episode might be a single, prolonged response to the stressor at work, or could it be the beginning of a recurrent pattern of depression for you?

I’m really not sure because I’ve never experienced anything like this before in my life. Right now, I am just too overwhelmed by my current situation and the stress from work to even think about whether this could happen again in the future.

Do you think that if you were able to find a way to cope with or resolve the feelings of worthlessness and guilt related to your work, you might be at risk of experiencing another episode like this in the future, or do you believe this is a one-time response to a specific set of circumstances?

I honestly don't know if this is just a one-time reaction or if it could happen again. Right now, I'm just too overwhelmed by this constant guilt and exhaustion to even think about the future. It's hard enough just trying to get through each day as it is.

Do you believe that the intense feelings of worthlessness and depression you're experiencing now could potentially be a part of a larger pattern of depression that might recur in the future, or do you think this is a singular response to the work-related stressor that triggered it?

I'm really not sure if this is part of a larger pattern or not. I haven't thought about it because I'm just too overwhelmed by how bad things have gotten over the last few months and the constant stress from work.

Given your experience of a single, prolonged episode of depression so far, do you think that if you were to recover from your current episode, you would be at risk of experiencing another episode of depression in response to future stressors or significant life changes?

I honestly don't know, and it's really hard for me to think about the future right now. I'm just so focused on trying to get through each day because everything feels so heavy and overwhelming in the present.

Do you think the fact that this is your first episode of depression, lasting about four months, might suggest that this could be a single episode of depression in response to a specific stressor, rather than a recurring pattern of depression?

Yes, this is indeed the first time I've ever gone through such a severe depression, and it's been going on for about four months now. It all started after the stress of my new promotion and that high-profile cheating investigation at the casino. I really hope it's just a reaction to this overwhelming situation, because I’ve never felt anything like this in my life.

Given that you've had a single episode of depression lasting about four months without previous episodes, do you think the duration and your response to the work-related stressor might suggest a difference between a single episode of depression and a potential recurrent depressive disorder?

I don't really know much about the clinical difference between a single episode and a recurrent disorder, but I do know this entire experience is completely new to me. I've never had these whispering voices or the feeling of being recorded before this depression hit four months ago. It really feels like a direct, overwhelming reaction to the intense stress I've been under at work.

Do you think that if you were to experience a significant reduction or resolution of your current depressive symptoms, you would still worry about having another episode like this in the future, or do you believe that would largely depend on how you cope with future stressors?
I haven't really thought about the future or how I would cope with other stressors down the road. Right now, I am just too overwhelmed and exhausted by how bad things are to think that far ahead.

Do you think that if your depressive symptoms were to significantly improve or resolve, you would still be concerned about the possibility of experiencing another episode of depression in the future, and if so, what do you think might trigger it?

I haven't really thought about the future or what might trigger another episode because I am just too consumed by my current feelings of worthlessness. Everything right now is so incredibly heavy and overwhelming that I can't even picture what lies ahead.

Do you think that the fact this is your first episode of depression, triggered by a specific work-related stressor and lasting about four months, might suggest it's a single episode rather than part of a recurring pattern?

Yes, I think that makes sense because I have never gone through anything like this before in my life. It has been one continuous, heavy episode that started right after the intense stress of that cheating investigation four months ago. Before that, I had absolutely no history of these kinds of feelings.

Do you think that if you were to recover from this episode of depression, the fact that it was triggered by a specific stressor and has lasted for about four months might suggest it is less likely to recur compared to if you had a history of similar episodes?

I really don't know how to answer that, since I don't understand how the clinical side of these things works. Right now, I'm just so overwhelmed by how awful I feel that I can't even think about the chances of it happening again.

Do you think the fact that your symptoms have been present for about four months without significant improvement suggests a more chronic condition, or do you believe they could still resolve with the right support or changes in your work environment?

These feelings have been going on continuously for about four months now, ever since that big cheating investigation at work. Honestly, it’s hard to imagine things ever getting better or resolving, even with support, because the guilt and fear feel so deeply ingrained now. I just feel completely hopeless about ever finding a way out of this darkness.

Do you think that if your current depressive episode were to resolve, you would be likely to experience another episode of similar severity in the future, or do you believe this is a one-time response to the extreme stress you've been under?

I honestly haven't thought about whether this will happen again because I can't even imagine getting past this current episode. Right now, I'm just too overwhelmed by my present feelings to think about the future at all.

Do you think the fact that you've had no previous episodes of depression and this episode was triggered by a specific work-related stressor suggests that this might be a single episode of depression, rather than a recurring pattern?

I'm really not sure how psychiatric diagnoses or patterns work, so I can't say if this is just a single episode. But I can definitely confirm that I have never experienced anything like this deep depression or these scary thoughts before the stress at work started. It is all completely new and terrifying to me.

Do you think that the lack of previous episodes and the clear trigger of the cheating investigation at work might suggest that this episode of depression could be a single, severe episode rather than the start of a recurring pattern of depression?

I really don't know anything about clinical patterns or if this will happen again, but I can tell you I've never felt this way in my entire life before now. I just desperately hope it's a one-time thing because this whole experience has been so incredibly heavy and overwhelming.

Do you think that the fact this is your first episode of depression, and it has been ongoing for about four months, suggests it could be a single episode of depression rather than part of a recurring pattern?

Yes, I think that makes sense because I have never experienced anything like this in my entire life before. It has just been one continuous, unbroken struggle for the past four months since that investigation at work. It doesn't feel like a recurring pattern, just one long, heavy nightmare that won't go away.

Do you think that if you were to recover from this episode of depression, the fact that it was your first episode and lasted about four months might suggest it is more likely to be a single episode rather than a recurrent depressive disorder?

I'm really not sure about those medical or diagnostic terms, since I don't have a medical background. I just really hope this is a one-time thing because these past four months have been incredibly painful and exhausting. I don't know how to predict if it will happen again.

Do you think that if you were able to find a way to cope with or resolve the feelings of worthlessness and guilt related to your work, you would still be at risk of experiencing another episode like this in the future?

I'm really not sure about that because it's hard to imagine ever getting past these feelings of guilt and worthlessness right now. I haven't thought about the future or what might happen later; I'm just trying to get through each day.
